chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Muammar ibn Khallad, who said:

Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), whenever he ate, would be brought a platter which was placed near his table. He would select the best of the foods that were brought, take a bit of each, and place them in that platter. Then he would order for it to be given to the poor.
But he will not attempt the uphill road
Then he would say: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knew that not every human being is able to emancipate a neck, so He made for them the way to Paradise.'

key_terms.عِتْقِ رَقَبَةٍ: Emancipation of a neck (freeing a slave)
key_terms.فَلَا اقْتَحَمَ الْعَقَبَةَ: But he will not attempt the uphill road

ai.seo_question: How does Imam Al-Rida (peace be upon him) connect feeding the poor to the concept of 'attempting the uphill road' in Surah Al-Balad?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Al-Rida (AS) demonstrates the virtue of *Ihsan* (excellence) in charity by selecting the finest portions of food for the poor, directly linking this act to Surah Al-Balad. He elucidates that since freeing a slave is a high-tier expiation (*Kaffarah*) inaccessible to all, feeding the hungry serves as a spiritually equivalent and accessible path to Paradise, reflecting the Shia emphasis on practical piety. This practice underscores the theological concept that charitable deeds are a means of spiritual elevation and divine proximity.
